body.en: Mechanics begins with motion in a straight line under constant acceleration.
For constant acceleration: \( v=u+at \), \( s=ut+\tfrac12 at^{2} \), \( v^{2}=u^{2}+2as \). Velocity is the derivative of displacement; acceleration the derivative of velocity.

Proportional Invariance, Linear Structure & Quantitative Modeling: Across Cambridge International AS Level (9709 Paper 1 / Paper 4 / Paper 5), multi-step problems reduce to identifying invariant quantities—constant rates of change \(m = \dfrac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}\), conservation of total work/mass, or linear system rank conditions. A two-variable linear system \(a_1 x + b_1 y = c_1\), \(a_2 x + b_2 y = c_2\) has a unique intersection if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} \ne \dfrac{b_1}{b_2}\), no solution (parallel lines) if \(\dfrac{a_1}{a_2} = \dfrac{b_1}{b_2} \ne \dfrac{c_1}{c_2}\), and infinitely many solutions if all three ratios coincide.

body.en:
SUVAT vs Calculus: SUVAT formulas apply ONLY when acceleration is constant. If velocity or acceleration varies with time (e.g. \(v = 3t^2 - 12t\)), SUVAT yields zero marks — you must differentiate (\(a = \frac{dv}{dt}\)) or integrate (\(s = \int v\,dt\)).

Velocity-Time graphs: Gradient equals acceleration (\(a = \frac{\Delta v}{\Delta t}\)). Total area under the graph equals displacement. For distance vs displacement: if the graph drops below the time axis (negative velocity), distance sums the absolute areas, whereas displacement nets them.

Vertical motion sign convention: Fix a reference direction at the start (usually upwards positive). Under this convention, acceleration is \(a = -g = -9.8\text{ m/s}^2\) (or \(-9.81\)). Any position below the launch point corresponds to negative displacement \(s < 0\).

Why Successive Multipliers & Harmonic Average Speed Work: If a quantity \(Q_0\) undergoes a percentage change \(p\%\) followed by \(q\%\), the compound multiplier is the product of individual scale factors:

\[ Q_{\text{final}} = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p}{100}\right)\!\left(1 + \frac{q}{100}\right) = Q_0\left(1 + \frac{p + q}{100} + \frac{pq}{10000}\right) \]

Notice the cross term \(\dfrac{pq}{10000}\): an increase of \(p\%\) followed by a decrease of \(p\%\) yields \(Q_0\bigl(1 - (p/100)^2\bigr) < Q_0\). Similarly, traveling equal distance \(d\) at speeds \(v_1\) and \(v_2\) takes total time \(T = \frac{d}{v_1} + \frac{d}{v_2}\), so average speed is the harmonic mean \(v_{\text{avg}} = \dfrac{2d}{d/v_1 + d/v_2} = \dfrac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

A particle moves so that its velocity at time \(t\) s is \(v=3t^2-12t+9\) m/s. Find (a) the acceleration at \(t=2\), (b) when the particle is momentarily at rest.

(a) \(a=\dfrac{dv}{dt}=6t-12\). At \(t=2\): \(a=0\) m/s².

(b) \(v=0\Rightarrow3(t-1)(t-3)=0\Rightarrow t=1\) s or \(t=3\) s.

Problem (Hard): A particle \( T \) moves in a straight line with initial velocity \( u = 21\text{ m s}^{-1} \) and constant acceleration \( a = 19\text{ m s}^{-2} \) over time \( a = 5\text{ s} \). Hence find the final velocity \( B(a) = u + aa \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Using \( v = u + at = 21 + (19)(5) = 116 \).

Problem (Easy): A particle \( T \) starts with speed \( u = 4\text{ m s}^{-1} \) and constant acceleration \( a = 6\text{ m s}^{-2} \) for \( a = 10\text{ s} \). Hence find the displacement \( B(a) = ua + \frac{1}{2}aa^2 \).

Step-by-Step Solution: Using \( s = (4)(10) + (3)(10^2) = 340 \).

Dividing by a negative number reverses order on the real number line.
Flip the inequality symbol whenever multiplying or dividing by a negative: \(x < -4\).
Computing round-trip average speed as \(\frac{v_1 + v_2}{2}\)
Time spent at the slower speed is longer than time spent at the faster speed.
Use total distance over total time: \(v_{\text{avg}} = \frac{2v_1 v_2}{v_1 + v_2}\).

body.en: High-Speed Exam Shortcut (Cambridge International AS Level (9709 Paper 1 / Paper 4 / Paper 5)): When a linear system asks for a combined expression like \(3x + 3y\) rather than \(x\) and \(y\) individually, add or subtract the two equations directly before isolating either variable—this often yields the target expression in a single step.

question.en: A train accelerates uniformly from rest to \(30\text{ m/s}\) in \(20\text{ s}\), travels at constant speed \(30\text{ m/s}\) for \(60\text{ s}\), and then decelerates uniformly to rest in \(15\text{ s}\). Find: (a) the acceleration in the first phase, (b) the total distance travelled, (c) the average speed for the entire journey.

solution.en:
(a) \(a_1 = \dfrac{v - u}{t} = \dfrac{30 - 0}{20} = 1.5\text{ m/s}^2\).
(b) Total distance is the area of the trapezoid on the \(v\)-\(t\) graph with parallel sides \(60\text{ s}\) and \(20 + 60 + 15 = 95\text{ s}\), and height \(30\text{ m/s}\): \[s = \dfrac{60 + 95}{2} \times 30 = \dfrac{155}{2} \times 30 = 155 \times 15 = 2325\text{ m}\] (c) Average speed: \[\text{Average speed} = \dfrac{\text{Total distance}}{\text{Total time}} = \dfrac{2325\text{ m}}{95\text{ s}} \approx 24.47\text{ m/s} \approx 24.5\text{ m/s (3 s.f.)}\]

hints.en: Tier 1 (Conceptual Setup): Identify the governing relationship in Kinematics and start from \(30\text{ m/s}\).
Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(a_1 = \dfrac{v - u}{t} = \dfrac{30 - 0}{20} = 1.5\text{ m/s}^2\).
Tier 3 (Final Verification): Check signs, units, and domain restrictions on your result before opening the full solution below.

question.en: A stone is thrown vertically upwards with speed \(15\text{ m/s}\) from the top of a cliff \(40\text{ m}\) above sea level. Taking \(g = 9.8\text{ m/s}^2\) and upwards as positive: (a) find the maximum height reached above the cliff, (b) calculate the time taken for the stone to reach the sea.

solution.en: (a) At maximum height, \(v = 0\). \(u = +15\text{ m/s}\), \(a = -9.8\text{ m/s}^2\): \[v^2 = u^2 + 2as \Rightarrow 0 = 15^2 + 2(-9.8)s \Rightarrow 19.6s = 225 \Rightarrow s = \dfrac{225}{19.6} \approx 11.48\text{ m} \approx 11.5\text{ m}\] (b) At the sea, the displacement relative to the launch point is \(s = -40\text{ m}\). Use \(s = ut + \tfrac{1}{2}at^2\): \[-40 = 15t + \tfrac{1}{2}(-9.8)t^2 \Rightarrow -40 = 15t - 4.9t^2 \Rightarrow 4.9t^2 - 15t - 40 = 0\] Solve via quadratic formula: \[t = \dfrac{15 \pm \sqrt{(-15)^2 - 4(4.9)(-40)}}{2(4.9)} = \dfrac{15 \pm \sqrt{225 + 784}}{9.8} = \dfrac{15 \pm \sqrt{1009}}{9.8}\] Since \(\sqrt{1009} \approx 31.765\), and \(t > 0\): \[t = \dfrac{15 + 31.765}{9.8} = \dfrac{46.765}{9.8} \approx 4.77\text{ s (3 s.f.)}\]

Tier 2 (Key Transformation): Apply the key algebraic/geometric step leading toward \(v = 0\).
